source.title: Manzanilla, López & Freter 1996, Dating Results From Excavations in Quarry Tunnels Behind the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan

findings.subject: Quarry-tunnel plan and occupation sequence
findings.assertion: Excavations documented four separate quarry tunnels 200–270 m east of the Sun Pyramid: Cueva de la Basura, de las Varillas, del Pirul, and del Camino. Deposits include roughly one metre of recent and Postclassic sediment over disintegrated tuff fill containing Teotihuacan pottery, slate and human remains; a scoria layer occurs in Cueva de la Basura.
findings.limitation: These are tunnels east of the pyramid, not the distinct cave under the Sun Pyramid. Date of quarrying is inferred.

findings.subject: Early radiocarbon and mixed quarry deposits
findings.assertion: The Cueva de la Basura assemblage includes mica, polychrome pottery, lithics, onyx pendants, cut/rounded human skulls and Prunus capuli seeds, with dates near AD 350–550 for some material. Sample Beta-69912 has an approximate calibrated average near AD 80, cautiously associated with possible extraction activity.
findings.limitation: The full calibration interval and original sample context remain to verify; this is not a direct Sun Pyramid construction date.

findings.subject: Cueva de las Varillas funerary chamber
findings.assertion: Thirteen burials were reported, including three seated adults facing south around a pillar and seven newborns in a central chamber beneath a ceiling opening. Vessels and projectile-point offerings accompanied burials; associated samples Beta-75377 and Beta-75381 averaged around AD 930.
findings.limitation: An Aztec intrusion is reported for another date; water-pouring through roof opening remains hypothetical.

findings.subject: Varillas storage bin bases
findings.assertion: The excavators recorded 13 circular storage-bin bases, seven around a burial area and six in an inner chamber approximately 50 metres from the entrance. Some contained Chenopodium, Amaranthus or maize remains. Figure 14 records sandal, foot and hand impressions in a leveled floor.
findings.limitation: Plant-specific laboratory evidence and proposed fertility rituals require independent review.

findings.subject: Cueva del Pirul child burials and dogs
findings.assertion: Fourteen burials included two seated adults, two flexed young adults, four children and six perinatal individuals. Three articulated dogs (two adults and a puppy) lay near child and newborn burials; two dogs are photographed near children in Figure 18. Distinct later Aztec activity dates near AD 1410–1435.
findings.limitation: The meaning of the dogs as underworld guides is interpretation; Figure 19 not inspected; avoid mixing burial and late-Aztec phases.
